title: A Machine for the Gravity
premise: Rosalind Villalobos has spent eleven years as the sole caretaker of the Meridian Seed Vault, ferrying supplies between Earth and the silent orbital arks on a route officially decommissioned after the Sundering split humanity into ground-dwellers and sleepers. When she finds the name 'E. Villalobos' on the manifest of the Halcyon—a ship that never flew—she learns her dead brother may be alive in cryosleep aboard an unregistered ark, and that her own caretaker contract was designed to keep one witness close to the vault's true purpose: a kill-switch that will decide which half of humanity wakes. Hunted by the Ark Authority and courted by the ground-born Concord, Rosalind must choose between reviving the sleeping millions or the surface survivors whose water is already failing—and discovers the choice was rigged long ago by the same people who erased her brother. In the end she refuses both factions, burns the kill-switch's authority by waking every sleeper at once, and accepts that survival without consent is just another kind of extinction.
about_author: Mara Coldharbour is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent six years writing route manifests for Antarctic supply runs before turning to fiction. She writes slow-burn science fiction about people who keep systems running after everyone else has stopped believing in them.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Establishes her solitary life running supply hops between the abandoned seed vault and derelict relay stations, talking to archived voices to stay sane. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness masking grief for her brother Elias, lost in the Sundering evacuations.

chapters.title: Manifest of a Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. During a routine cargo audit she finds 'E. Villalobos' listed on the Halcyon, a vessel with no flight history, docked at coordinates no chart admits exist. Emotional beat: the floor drops out of her ordered world; hope arrives as an error.

chapters.title: What the Vault Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. She descends into the vault's sealed sublevels seeking records and finds a console keyed to her biometrics—one only she can arm. Emotional beat: dawning horror that her isolation was engineered.

chapters.title: The Man from the Concord
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A ground-born envoy named Teodor Okafor intercepts her shuttle, offering protection and answers in exchange for the vault's access codes. Emotional beat: first human contact in years, laced with the suspicion of being wanted rather than seen.

chapters.title: Authority
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. An Ark Authority cruiser demands she surrender the vault; its commander, Ilsa Reyes, claims the sleepers' survival depends on it. Emotional beat: realizing both factions need her as a tool, not a person.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: POV flashbacks woven through present-day repair work. Reconstructs the Sundering: the evacuation, the lie that no ships were lost, the last message from Elias. Emotional beat: memory as both wound and compass.

chapters.title: Coordinates That Don't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Defying both factions, she plots a course to the Halcyon's phantom berth using Elias's childhood star-charts as a cipher key. Emotional beat: loyalty overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. She boards the Halcyon: a fully crewed ark hidden mid-route, thousands in cryosleep, its logs falsified by someone inside the Authority. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Pod 4471
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. She finds Elias's pod—occupied, vitals green, wake-date set fifty years out. Beside it, a note in his handwriting warning her not to trust the manifest. Emotional beat: reunion impossible, love preserved like the seeds above.

chapters.title: Okafor's Truth
chapters.summary: POV dual: Rosalind and Teodor. He confesses the Concord knows about the kill-switch and wants the sleepers kept under forever—the surface can't sustain them. Emotional beat: sympathy for an unforgivable position.

chapters.title: Reyes's Truth
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Reyes reveals the Authority's counter-plan: wake the sleepers, abandon the surface, let the ground-born die of thirst. Each faction holds half the arithmetic. Emotional beat: the sickening symmetry of genocide.

chapters.title: The Rigged Choice
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Deciphering the vault console, she finds the kill-switch was never neutral—it's coded to favor whichever faction delivers her codes first. Her invisibility was the design. Emotional beat: rage at being made an instrument.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The Authority disables her ship to trap her at the vault; Teodor smuggles her parts, deepening their uneasy alliance. Emotional beat: trust built in the space between betrayals.

chapters.title: Voices in the Archive
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Searching the vault's comm archives for evidence, she finds recorded orders proving Elias discovered the plot years ago and was silenced, not lost. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Water Clock
chapters.summary: POV Teodor. His POV chapter shows the Concord's failing aquifers and the desperation driving them; he begins secretly feeding Rosalind data. Emotional beat: a man choosing conscience over tribe.

chapters.title: Siege at Meridian
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Both factions converge on the vault; Reyes offers Elias's immediate revival if Rosalind arms the switch for the Authority. Emotional beat: the offer aimed exactly at her weakest point.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Alone in the seed vault among ten thousand years of stored futures, she weighs consent against salvation and realizes neither faction ever asked anyone. Emotional beat: stillness before the storm; the theme crystallized.

chapters.title: The Arm
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Under siege, she initiates the wake sequence—but rewrites its targeting so it cannot discriminate: every pod, every ark, all at once, consent returned to the sleepers themselves. Emotional beat: climax; defiance as authorship.

chapters.title: Halcyon Rising
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. As pods open across the fleet, chaos and wonder erupt; Reyes moves to seize the vault by force while Teodor's defection turns the Concord's guns aside. Emotional beat: the world remade in real time, terrifying and alive.

chapters.title: Brother
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Elias wakes disoriented into a war zone; their reunion lasts minutes before he chooses to stand with her against Reyes's final assault. Emotional beat: joy and sorrow braided; the answer to eleven years of silence.

chapters.title: The Kill-Switch Dies
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. She physically destroys the console, ending the rigged choice forever, as Reyes must decide whether to fire on the woman who freed everyone—including her own sleeper family. Emotional beat: climax resolution through moral checkmate, not victory.

chapters.title: A Machine for the Gravity
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Months later, wakers and ground-born negotiate over failing water while Rosalind returns to tending seeds—now for a species learning to share. She keeps running the long route, but no longer alone. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; survival finally priced honestly.
